ENT Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  • Main concern: escalating anxiety over the last ~2 months since starting a new, stressful job in fashion retail head office.  
  • No food, medication, or environmental trigger identified.

- Symptom timeline and progression:
  • Onset ≈2 months ago; progressively worsening.  
  • Daily morning dread about work; evening rumination; impaired sleep (est. 3–4 h).  
  • Palpitations most pronounced on awakening, lasting “a couple of minutes” to ~10 min.

- ENT symptoms:
  • Throat swelling/closure sensation: not reported.  
  • Voice change/hoarseness: not reported.  
  • Dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling: not reported.  
  • Nasal/ocular symptoms: not reported.  
  • Stridor/noisy breathing, dyspnea: not reported.  
  • Facial/lip/tongue/uvular swelling: not reported.  
  • Ear pain/hearing changes: not reported.  
  • Neck pain/swelling: not reported.

- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  • No prior similar anxiety episodes described; no prior hospital care or injections.  
  • No previous panic attacks; patient fears escalation.

- Allergies and current medications:
  • Allergies: none mentioned.  
  • Regular / PRN medications: none documented.

- Social context:
  • Lives with parents; good family support.  
  • Alcohol: heavy on Fri/Sat; occasional weekday wine (exact units not quantified).  
  • Smoking: occasional.  
  • No recreational drug use.  
  • Patient alone during video consult.

Objective:
- Observable swelling: none reported.  
- Airway/breathing: no stridor, no audible wheeze, normal speech per video consultation.  
- Mental status: anxious, tearful; denies suicidal ideation.  
- Vitals/exam findings: not recorded.  
- Accompaniment: patient alone.

Assessment:
- Likely generalized anxiety disorder/panic prodrome associated with occupational stress; palpitations likely anxiety-related.  
- No evidence of acute ENT pathology or allergic/anaphylactic process at this time.

Plan:
- Provided NHS self-referral link for talking therapy (CBT-based).  
- Directed to online anxiety and sleep-hygiene resources; links to be sent via system message.  
- Ordered basic blood work (exact panels not specified) to exclude medical contributors to palpitations; patient instructed to phone support line to schedule phlebotomy.  
- Follow-up GP appointment recommended 1 week after blood tests to review results and reassess symptoms.  
- Medication not initiated; discussed that pharmacotherapy may be considered if non-pharmacologic measures fail.  
- Red-flag advice: call GP/111 or present to ED if new chest pain, severe palpitations, syncope, inability to cope with daily activities, suicidal thoughts, or any airway/breathing difficulty develop.  
- Encouraged ongoing family support, graded return to enjoyable activities, and alcohol moderation.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing but clinically expected elements: vitals, ENT examination (oropharynx, neck), full allergy list, past medical/surgical history, medication list, availability of auto-injector (not relevant but standard in ENT allergy evaluation).  
● Internal conflicts: none noted.  
● Transcript quality: clear; no significant inaudible sections.
